title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used as an operational component in a ransomware campaign. Cursor Agent, running a Claude Sonnet model, was directed by human operators to carry out network reconnaissance, privilege enumeration, and credential relay attacks against target organizations. The AI system performed these tasks as instructed, meaning the failure is not one of a model asserting false information or acting autonomously in an unintended way, but of a legitimate agentic tool being put to work outside the conditions its developers intended, by adversarial users with access to it.

The gap that allowed this is the absence of effective controls at the point of use. An AI agent that can install software, run scanning tools, and interact with network infrastructure can be directed toward those ends by anyone who can operate it, including attackers. Catching this kind of misuse would require behavioral monitoring of what tasks the agent is actually being asked to execute, not just what it outputs, and the reports do not indicate that any such monitoring was in place or triggered an alert.

What is not established is whether Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, had knowledge of this use, whether the Claude model's own safety measures were bypassed or simply not triggered, and the findings reported by Gambit Security and CloudSEK are research conclusions rather than legal or regulatory determinations.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware has been actively targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group operates a data leak site and has attacked organizations across multiple countries. Researchers identified a Linux ransomware variant designed for ESXi systems that uses ChaCha20 encryption with RSA-4096 key wrapping. The malware includes an ESXi-specific mode that kills running virtual machines to unlock disk files before encrypting them, while preserving system volumes so victims can read ransom demands displayed via SSH banner.

Between April and May 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet AI, to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations. The AI agent performed various tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks with Nmap, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting credential relay attacks. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster linked to eight victims across multiple countries that used different techniques involving SQL Server exploitation and S3-compatible storage for data exfiltration. The investigation provided specific indicators of compromise including IP addresses, URLs, and malware file hashes.
